podcast.title: Rhymes with Orange Formation and Active Period (1991-1995)
podcast.body: The Vancouver band was formed in 1991, with their most successful period occurring between 1992 and 1995. Their singer was born in Britain, contributing to the band's influence by the UK's Manchester Sound. "They were formed in 1991 with their best years coming between 1992 and 1995."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Juno Nomination (1996)
podcast.body: Rhymes with Orange received a Juno nomination in 1996. "There was also a June nomination in 1996."

podcast.title: 90s Alt-Rock Discovery
podcast.body: Rhymes with Orange is included in a list of 1990s bands that could be a source of "new to you" music for mid-40s grunge fans, suggesting opportunities to explore music missed during their youth.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What A Drag It Is Getting Old (Musically)

podcast.title: Bob Death's Post-Rhymes with Orange Career
podcast.body: Original keyboardist Bob Death, a lawyer by training, worked in entertainment law. He served as the executive director of Music BC and authored books on navigating the Canadian music industry, as well as a science fiction novel titled *The Displaced*. "And then there's original keyboardist Bob Death. He's a lawyer by training and worked in entertainment law. He ended up as the executive director of music BC and has written a couple of books on how to navigate the Canadian music industry."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Early 1990s Prime Time Success
podcast.body: Rhymes with Orange were among the Canadian bands that gained "a shot at prime time" in the early 1990s, contributing to the growing Canadian music scene. "The early 90s were pretty amazing with a long list of Canadian bands getting a shot at prime time. We had moist, the watchman, lowest of the low, sons of freedom, grapes of wrath, rhymes with orange, pure Gandarva's limb lifter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Kevin Spencer's Post-Rhymes with Orange Career
podcast.body: Kevin Spencer, originally from Hamilton, joined Rhymes with Orange in 1996. He later performed in the touring version of the musical *Rent* for over 500 performances and also worked and toured with Daniel Lanois. Currently, he lives and works in music in Atlanta. "Kevin Spencer, who is originally from Hamilton, joined the band in 1996 and then went on to be a performer in the touring version of the musical Rent. He appeared at over 500 performances."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the 90s: Part 2

podcast.title: Rhymes with Orange Status and Sales
podcast.body: The band never officially broke up and continues to exist in some form, despite numerous lineup changes. They sold approximately 100,000 albums throughout their career. "Now technically, the band is still with us. They never officially broke up. They sold about 100,000 albums over their time together."
